Laconia.wildlife_intro:
Laconia blends a working small city with a busy lakefront, and both sides call us. Downtown and Lakeport's older homes get bats, raccoons, gray squirrels and mice, while Weirs Beach cottages and shoreline homes open each spring to overwinter mice, bat colonies and raccoon damage. Skunks and woodchucks work yards citywide, and the bays and river keep raccoons traveling the shore all season.

Bike Week and the summer season compress a lot of Laconia work into spring readiness and fall closing — our crew seals lake properties in fall so winter stays quiet, and inspects in spring before guests and family arrive. Year-round homes follow the standard pattern of fall exclusion and spring litters. Bat work follows the state window, with exclusion outside May 15 to August 15.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Laconia, NH?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing or cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts.  Simple single-entry squirrel jobs cost less than full attic exclusion or bat work, and we never quote a firm figure before seeing the structure.

faqs.q: Our Weirs Beach cottage has bats every summer. Can that be ended?
faqs.a: Yes, with properly timed exclusion. Colonies return to the same cottage because the entries stay open. Our crew maps the gaps, installs one-way exits after the August 15 restriction lifts, and seals every entry. Done completely, the colony relocates to natural roosts and does not return the next summer.

Fall closing done well is Alton's whole game: food out, gaps sealed, chimney capped. Our crew offers closing and opening inspections built for lake properties, and handles the bat colonies that summer reveals — with exclusion after the August 15 date, neatly timed before most owners close up for the season. That rhythm keeps Alton camps quiet winter after winter.
